raw_response:
I have farmed these 10.9 mu for 40 years. I never went to school, but I know my land by walking on it every day. I watch what my neighbors do, especially Old Wang and the others on the east side. If they had good luck last year, I do the same thing.

This year I will plant winter wheat on 4.5 mu. After the maize comes off in June, I plough deep and sow wheat in October. I buy improved wheat seed from the village supply shop — the same kind Old Wang bought last year, his wheat had fat full heads. Before ploughing I spread one bag of compound fertilizer on each mu. When the wheat turns green in March, I topdress with half a bag of urea per mu, and at jointing time I add another 20 jin urea per mu. I irrigate four times: once before the winter freeze, once at green-up, once when it shoots up tall, and once when the grain is filling. I spray pesticide twice, once for aphids and once for the rust that came two years ago. I expect about 900 jin per mu if the weather is fair.

On that same 4.5 mu, after wheat harvest in early June, I plant summer maize right away. I use hybrid seed, the yellow bag — everyone does now, you cannot get good yield without it. I rotary till fast and sow. I put down one bag of compound fertilizer per mu at planting, then at big trumpet stage I spread half a bag of urea per mu. I irrigate twice if July is dry. I spray twice for armyworm. I expect about 1,100 jin per mu.

I keep 3 mu for cotton. Cotton needs deep loose soil, so I plough in spring. I spread two cartloads of manure per mu and one bag of compound fertilizer. At flowering and again at boll-set, I topdress with half a bag of urea per mu each time. I irrigate three times. Cotton always has worms, so I spray four times — I hire the electric sprayer from the village. Last year I got 460 jin seed cotton on the 3 mu, so about 230 jin per mu. I hope for the same.

The sandy 2 mu near the well I plant with millet. Millet is easy and good for family porridge. I use the traditional seed I saved from last year. I rotary till in late spring, put three-quarters of a bag of compound fertilizer per mu, and broadcast the seed. I irrigate once, maybe twice if it is very dry. One spray for worms. I expect about 520 jin per mu.

The 1.4 mu by my house I keep for stevia. Three years ago a buyer came to the village saying the leaves sell for cash. I planted cuttings from last year’s roots. I spread one cart of manure on the whole plot in spring, and about half a bag of compound fertilizer per mu. I water it twice when I water my vegetables. One spray for aphids. Last year I picked about 300 jin fresh leaves per mu. This year I expect about the same.

I worry about costs every day. A bag of urea is 85 yuan now, compound fertilizer is 120 yuan. For the whole farm I will spend nearly 2,500 yuan on chemical fertilizer alone. But I would rather put a little too much than risk a bad harvest. If my family goes hungry, that is a disaster; wasting some fertilizer is just money. When I am unsure, I do what I did last year. Change is risky. I watch my neighbors. If Old Wang puts more on his wheat, I put more too.
